Kawal Singh) Challan No.271/2024 Cnr No.Dlst-02-004542-2024 Judgment Municipal Corporation Of Delhi ......... Complainant Versus M/S Apollo Pharmacy through its Ar Mr.Jayvardhan Binjola Shop No.D-82, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi. .............. Accused Offence punishable u nder Section - 417 read with Section - 416 of The Delhi Municipal Corporation Act,1957 1. By way of the present Judgment, this court shall dispose off challan bearing No. 271/2024, of Apollo Pharmacy located at shop no. D-82, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi dated 05.02.2024 against Mr. Jayvardhan Binjola (Authorised Representative of Apollo pharmacy), under section-417 of Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 (hereinafter referred to as "DMC Act"). BRIEF FACTS: 2.
texts.facts: Notice under section-251 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) was framed against the accused on the same day, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. It was the defence of the accused that the shop trade in pharmaceutical items and is being run, after taking a valid licence from the Drug Control Department as per the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Therefore, no licence from MCD is required to run the said pharmaceutical shop and he is not liable to pay any fine for not having any license under the DMC Act.
texts.arguments: 10. The counsel for the accused submitted that the shop in question is a pharmacy shop and is engaged in trade of pharmaceutical products apart from small quantity of cosmetics as well as baby food products. The counsel for the accused further stated that the shop is being run after taking a valid license from the Drug Control Department under the Drugs and Cosmetics act as well as from FSSAI. The counsel argued that as per Section-417 of DMC Act the accused is not required to get any license from the MCD since the pharmaceutical items falls under item-21 of the Eleven Schedule, which does not mentions sale or trade as one of the necessary criteria for obtaining licence. The second argument of the accused is that as per the proviso of section-417 the accused is given liberty to sell small quantity of cosmetics and food products thus, the provisions of the said section have not been violated by the accused person. The counsel for the accused has relied on a judgment pronounced by this court titled as SDMC vs M/S Apollo Hospital Enterprises Ltd. MCD Challan No. 36580 dated 22.08.2015 in support of his arguments. 11.

9. Coming to the present MCD challan, as per the statement of PW-1 the name of the shop is Apollo Pharmacy and the employee of the accused found at the shop had signed the challan.
The prosecution had examined PW-1 and it had precipitated from his testimony that challan Ex.PW1/A is generated by him.
PW-1 stated that apart from medicines, the accused was also selling other grocery items like baby food products and other food products as shown in Ex.PW1/C.
In his testimony PW-1 testified that the employee of the accused namely Mr. Nihaluddin at the shop signed the challan Ex.PW1/A.
PW-1 had denied all the suggestions put to him regarding absence of violation of DMC Act and non-requirement of the shop to get license from the MCD.

It is a well settled law that the entries in the Eleventh Schedule are in the nature of restraint on the trade by regulating and stipulating a requirement of license therefore, are to be interpreted in a restrictive manner.
The scope of each entries in the Schedule cannot be expanded by employing aids or explanations to it.

12. In view of above settled law, this court is of the opinion that there is merit in the argument of the accused and the accused does not require any license for 'trade' of pharmaceutical or medical products from his shop in question.
13. Now coming to the other argument of the accused that the shop of the accused can trade in cosmetics and baby food products, in small quantity as per the proviso to Section-417 of the DMC Act.
It is clear from bare perusal of the Section-417 that the permission of the Commissioner of the MCD is required for trade, storage and health purposes.

While the Commissioner may issue 'General Trade License' for all the purposes mention in Part-1 and 'Storage license' for those in Part-2 of the Eleventh Schedule as per section-417(1)(a) and (d) respectively.
It also has power to issue license to restrain certain activities so to prevent nuisance on account of it being dangerous to life, health and property under section-417(1)(b).
And for all this purpose the Commissioner has been given explicit power under Section-417(3) to fix fees to be paid in respect of premises licensed under sub-section (1).
